decisions.issues: The correction worked and broke nothing. v01, the current pick, gave Ramayyan a clear moustache, chin stubble and straight hair combed back, which doesn't match his sheet. v02 removes the moustache and stubble. It also gives him a bald, shining crown with a short ring of tight black curls, matching the sheet's hairline. His thin, sharp features and the long fingers turning the small dark stone are kept. A faint stipple on the upper lip remains, but it reads as skin shading, not a moustache. The hands are unchanged from v01 and anatomically sound. The setting matches 2.1: laterite shrine steps at sunset among coconut palms, with lamps, and the palm-leaf bundle and stylus beside him. There is no painted text and no anachronism. The single lettering line can sit in the sunset sky and palm area at the top right, clear of his face and hands. v01 is not kept as backup because it has the moustache fault.

Correction FIXED the target: in v02 the stylus and the bound bundle are gone. Ramayyan now holds one opened leaf in both hands at waist height while his head turns toward Varma. His hands are sound, and the rest of the frame matches v01. Ramayyan still matches his sheet: clean-shaven, bald crown, ring of curls. Varma has the bare head and the knot behind his LEFT ear, gold necklaces, cream mundu and his spear at the right edge. Minor new points, neither a reason to reject: (1) the leaf carries faint, blurred horizontal strokes that suggest incised writing, with no letterforms, and at page size they read as texture; (2) the leaf is a little broad and paper-like for a palm leaf. Carried over from v01: Varma sits in a carved cushioned chair on the dais instead of on the bare dais; the standing guard has loose hair, not a front topknot; one seated chief has a beard. The sky and sea between the pillars (roughly x 0.36-0.57, y 0.15-0.33) give clear space for the RAMAYYAN balloon. The backup, v01, still has the stylus and bundle fault this round was meant to fix. Use it only if v02 is rejected for the leaf strokes.

Kept the current pick v03 because the regeneration v04 BROKE the story beat. What v04 fixed: Nagoji now stands apart at the back by a far pillar, Varma sits on a low dais against a bolster, and his spear is at his right hand. What v04 broke: Ramayyan holds a stylus and a thick bound palm-leaf bundle and appears to be writing. He is not breaking the wax on the single sealed ola from 5.2. This is the same stylus and bundle fault that the 5.5 correction removed, so it would clash with 5.4 and 5.5. v04 also has smaller faults: Varma's hair is a big loose mane with the bun on the back of the crown, not a side knot above his left ear, and Nagoji's ear has a small gold drop hanging from it. v03 itself shows the beat correctly: Ramayyan, clean-shaven and matching his sheet, cracks a red wax seal on the ola. Varma's knot sits on his left side, the chiefs wear topknots and gold earrings, and there is no text or anachronism. v03 still has the problem the reviewer flagged: Nagoji stands at the right side about level with the king, not apart at the back, and Varma sits in a carved cushioned chair on a raised dais. Nagoji's ear is a tiny gold hoop rather than a flush stud, barely visible at page size. If another regeneration is wanted, start from the v04 composition and add: 'Ramayyan holds NO stylus and NO bound bundle: in both hands he holds one long narrow palm-leaf ola tied with cord, his thumbs cracking the red wax seal on it. Varma's hair is tied in a neat knot on the LEFT side of his head above his left ear, not a bun on the crown. Nagoji's ear has only a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it.'

The correction works. In v02 Varma has jet-black hair with no grey and a side knot above his LEFT ear. He sits cross-legged on the low dais holding the ola, with his spear leaning at his right hand, and he looks away from the chief. That matches the chapter 12 @5- row and panels 6.1, 6.3 and 6.5. The grey-haired Nair chief in the foreground is unchanged: grey topknot, heavy gold earring and a sound hand on his chest. The edit left no artifacts where the standing figure was removed; the dais steps and mat are clean. No new faults. Two minor points: Varma holds a folded stack of several leaves rather than the single strip seen in 6.3, and the map sheet on the table has faint scribble marks. These are carried over unchanged from v01, read as map lines and are not legible. The hall's open sea side matches the neighbouring panels. There is space for lettering in the sky between the pillars at top centre (CHIEF) and in the sky above Varma at top right (VARMA x2). v01 is rejected as a backup because Varma there has greying hair and stands instead of sitting on the dais, the very faults this correction fixed.

I kept v02. The v03 regeneration fixes the staging but breaks the ear hard check, so it cannot replace v02.

What v03 fixes: Nagoji is seen from behind, walking off the rise toward the camp fires and tents at the left. The long, pale, empty beach and the moonlit black sea now run open across the right half of the frame, and the whole upper-middle and right sky is clear for the caption. The commander sheet is correct: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, broad red sash, cream trousers, laced boots and a talwar at the left hip. Hands are sound and there is no text.

What v03 breaks: a small gold drop hangs below the stud on his right earlobe. Zoom at about (720,167) for the stud and (721,174) for the drop in the 2172x724 frame, with a gold link between them. This is the same hanging-drop fault that failed v01. v03 also adds two new red-orange pennants on poles over the camp tents, at about x 0.16 to 0.23 and y 0.29 to 0.39. They read like the saffron Maratha pennant, which the script allows only in memory and vision panels (2.5, 4.4, 8.3). Panel 8.1's camp flies a plain white flag.

State of v02: the ear passes, with a tiny flush stud and nothing hanging. The chin is clean-shaven under a thick curled moustache, and the costume is right. Its known weaknesses remain. He faces the camera as he walks past the fires instead of being seen from behind. The men at the camp wear turbans and tunics rather than the bare-headed Nairs of 8.1. The beach curve sits in the lower-middle and right, so the caption must be lettered wide and shallow in the upper-middle sky (about x 0.35 to 0.95, top 40%) to keep the sand visible.

Recommendation: v03 is the better composition. An ear-region edit to a flush stud with nothing hanging, as was done for v01 to v02, plus removing the two red-orange pennants or recolouring them to the plain white of 8.1, would likely make it the pick on re-review.

panels.missing: Nagoji walks toward the viewer with every camp fire behind him, and his head is turned to look out at the sea, so he has not turned from the sea and is not walking back toward the fires. The script needs him facing away from the sea and heading into the firelight, for example seen from behind or in profile walking toward the camp, so the panel carries 'I turned back toward the camp.'
